narrative.intro: Granite Construction recorded $607M in contract obligations for FY2026 to date, from 14 awards that average $43.4M each. Obligations are up 152.6% year over year. The Department of Homeland Security is the dominant buyer, obligating $545M. Commercial and Institutional Building Construction is the largest market by obligation, with $545M. Highway, Street, and Bridge Construction and Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction follow, with $35.9M and $26.4M respectively. Historical obligations show a recent rise from $20.3M in FY21, $19.7M in FY22, $335M in FY23, $185M in FY24, and $240M in FY25 to the current $607M in FY26. The fiscal-year-to-date totals are partial, so FY2026 figures cover only the current portion of the year. Award-count and award-size figures reflect counted awards and average award value to date, not full-year totals. Use the agency and NAICS breakdowns for pipeline and capture work focused on federal construction and infrastructure contracting.

sections.heading: Who are the main federal buyers of Granite Construction?
sections.body: The Department of Homeland Security obligated $545M for Granite Construction in FY2026 to date. The Department of Transportation obligated $35.9M and the Department of Defense obligated $26.7M. These three agencies represent the top buyers and account for the bulk of current-year obligations.

sections.heading: Which markets and contract types drive Granite Construction's federal work?
sections.body: Commercial and Institutional Building Construction accounts for $545M in obligations for Granite Construction. Highway, Street, and Bridge Construction accounts for $35.9M and Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction accounts for $26.4M. Asphalt Paving Mixture and Block Manufacturing accounts for $250K, showing concentrated federal demand in construction and civil works.

faq.q: How much does Granite Construction make from federal contracts?
faq.a: Granite Construction recorded $607M in federal contract obligations for FY2026 to date. Granite Construction received 14 awards so far this fiscal year, with an average award size of $43.4M and obligations up 152.6% year over year. Historical fiscal-year totals include $20.3M in FY21, $19.7M in FY22, $335M in FY23, $185M in FY24, and $240M in FY25.

faq.q: Which agencies buy from Granite Construction?
faq.a: The Department of Homeland Security is the largest buyer, obligating $545M to Granite Construction in FY2026 to date. The Department of Transportation obligated $35.9M and the Department of Defense obligated $26.7M. These three agencies are the top federal customers for the current fiscal-year-to-date period.

faq.q: What does Granite Construction sell to the government?
faq.a: Granite Construction sells federal construction and civil works services, led by Commercial and Institutional Building Construction with $545M in obligations. Granite Construction also sells Highway, Street, and Bridge Construction services with $35.9M and Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction services with $26.4M. Granite Construction has $250K in obligations in Asphalt Paving Mixture and Block Manufacturing.

faq.q: Which Granite Construction contracts are expiring soon?
faq.a: Expired or expiring contract details are not listed as line items in the provided figures, so specific expiring contracts are not shown.
